chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah. He said: Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Madini narrated to me. He said: Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father Muhammad ibn Ali from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali from his father Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said:

I visited the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in the Quba Mosque, and with him was a group of his companions. When he caught sight of me, his face became radiant and he smiled, until I saw the shining whiteness of his teeth. Then he said: To me, O Ali! To me, O Ali! He kept drawing me closer until my thigh touched his thigh.

Then he turned to his companions and said: O my companions! Mercy has come to you with the coming of Ali, my brother, to you. O my companions! Truly, Ali is from me and I am from Ali. His spirit is from my spirit and his clay is from my clay. He is my brother, my deputy, and my vicegerent over my Nation in my lifetime and after my death. Whoever obeys him has obeyed me, whoever supports him has supported me, and whoever opposes him has opposed me.

key_terms.خَلِيفَة: khalifah — vicegerent, successor, representative; here designating Ali as the Prophet's successor over the Muslim community
key_terms.طِينَة: tinah — clay, primordial nature; the idea that great souls share a common spiritual origin from the same divine clay
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ قُبَاءَ: Quba Mosque — the first mosque built in Islam, near Medina, considered a sacred site
key_terms.مَعَاشِر: ma'ashir — O assembly of, O gathering of; a term of address used when speaking to a group
key_terms.وَصِيّ: wasi — deputy, executor of will, legatee; in Shia theology, the designated successor of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali's spiritual unity and his appointment as vicegerent in the Quba Mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Ali ibn Abi Talib's firsthand account of a visit to the Prophet at Quba Mosque, where the Prophet publicly declared his profound spiritual union with Ali—describing their spirits and natures as one—and formally appointed Ali as his brother, deputy, and vicegerent over the Muslim community both during the Prophet's life and after his death. The proclamation 'Ali is from me and I am from Ali' is one of the most celebrated Prophetic sayings establishing Ali's unique spiritual and political authority. This narration was transmitted through the chain of Imams (silsilat al-dhahab, 'golden chain'), lending it exceptional authority in Shia tradition.
